issues.legal_issue: The bar on further appeals from a single judge’s decision does not retrospectively extinguish an intra-court appeal filed before the bar came into force.
material_facts: A probate suit was dismissed, and the beneficiary’s first appeal was dismissed by a single judge of the High Court in 1992.
The beneficiary filed an intra-court appeal against the single judge’s decision before the 2002 amendment to the Code of Civil Procedure came into force on 1 July 2002.
The division bench allowed the intra-court appeal, and the opposing party challenged that ruling before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The intra-court appeal filed before the amendment came into force was maintainable because Section 100A did not apply retrospectively. The Supreme Court dismissed the challenge to the division bench’s ruling.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100A of the Code of Civil Procedure, as substituted by the 2002 amendment, bars a further appeal from a single judge’s decision in the cases it covers. A right of appeal is a substantive, vested right, which cannot be taken away retrospectively without express enactment or necessary implication. The Court relied on Messrs. Hoosein Kasam Dada (India) Ltd. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, Shiv Shakti Co-op. Housing Society v. Swaraj Developers, P.S. Sathappan v. Andhra Bank Ltd., Kamal Kumar Dutta v. Ruby General Hospital Ltd., and Bento De Souza Egipsy v. Yvette Alvares Colaco and Sanjay Z. Rane v. Saibai S. Dubaxi, which support the vested-right principle or the prospective operation of Section 100A.

predicates.intra_court_appeal_from_single_judge_dec: A party brought an intra-court appeal against a decision made by a single judge of a High Court.
predicates.appeal_filed_before_new_bar_took_effect: The party filed the intra-court appeal before the statutory bar on further appeals took effect.
predicates.intra_court_appeal_is_maintainable: The intra-court appeal may proceed despite the later statutory bar.

issues.definition: When a party brings an intra-court appeal against a single judge’s decision before the new bar takes effect, that appeal remains maintainable.
